en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Seventeenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to a Buddha Bears Great Fruit:
Should it not be said that what is given to a Buddha bears great fruit?
“Yes.

“But is it not true that the Blessed One is the foremost of bipeds, the best of bipeds, the deliverer of bipeds, the supreme of bipeds, the excellent of bipeds—the peerless, the equal of the unequaled, the matchless, the incomparable, the one without a rival?
“Yes.”
If the Blessed One is indeed the foremost of bipeds, the best of bipeds, the most excellent of bipeds,
the supreme of bipeds, the preeminent of bipeds— the peerless, the equal of the unequaled, the matchless, the incomparable, the one without a rival— then indeed, it should be said:
"What is given to a Buddha bears great fruit."
Is it not to be said that "what is given to a Buddha bears great fruit"?
Yes, it is so.
Is there anyone equal to the Buddha—
in virtue, in concentration, or in wisdom?
There is none.
If there is indeed no one equal to the Buddha—
in virtue, in concentration, and in wisdom— then indeed, sir, it should be said:
"What is given to the Buddha yields great fruit."
Is it not to be said that "what is given to a Buddha bears great fruit"?
Yes, it is so.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Neither in this world nor in the world beyond is there found anyone equal or superior to the Buddha”?
"He has reached the preeminence among those worthy of offerings,
who seek great fruit for their merit"—
is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes.
“In that case, what is given to the Buddha is of great fruit.
Thus ends the discussion: “It should not be said that what is given to the Buddha is of great fruit.”
